newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to step up security over islands threat.
newsitem.headline: China says to step up security over islands threat.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it would tighten security for its citizens after its de facto embassy in Hong Kong reported receiving a threatening letter from Japanese rightwingers over a group of disputed islands.

"The Chinese side will take action at home to strengthen our security," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a briefing in Beijing, adding that he hoped other countries would also protect Chinese citizens.
He did not give further details.

Tension over the disputed East China Sea islands, known in China as the Diaoyus and in Japan as the Senkakus, soared on Monday when Hong Kong and Taiwan activists pierced a Japanese cordon and planted Chinese and Taiwan flags on one of them.

Zhang Junsheng, a deputy director of the Xinhua news agency's Hong Kong branch, which acts as Beijing's de facto embassy in the British colony, said the agency had received a threatening letter from Japanese rightists.
"This (rightwing) organisation has not only threatened to kill and harm Chinese people, our Xinhua branch in Hong Kong has also received a threatening letter," Zhang told reporters.
Asked what China would do to protect its government officials, spokesman Shen said all "relevant" countries should protect Chinese citizens in line with international norms, but gave no details.
